bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to "North Dakota Field Office Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan".
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution nullifies the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) relating to the Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan (RMP) for the North Dakota Field Office and issued on January 8, 2025. By way of background, an RMP guides the management of lands administered by BLM. The 2025 North Dakota RMP modified the 1988 RMP, including by limiting development of oil and gas in low-potential areas and new coal leasing to areas within four miles of existing mines.

classification.plainSummary: This joint resolution would overturn a Bureau of Land Management rule issued in January 2025 that updated how federal lands in North Dakota are managed. The 2025 rule restricted new oil and gas development in areas with low potential and limited new coal leasing to locations within four miles of existing mines. If this resolution passes, those restrictions would be nullified and the earlier 1988 management plan would remain in effect.

industries.rationale: The bill would nullify restrictions on oil, gas, and coal development on federal lands in North Dakota.
The bill would remove limits on new coal leasing that currently restrict operations to areas near existing mines.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would cancel the rule submitted by the federal land agency relating to the Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan for the North Dakota Field Office and issued on January 8, 2025.
plain.whoItTouches: People who live near or work on federal land. People who live near a mine, and people who work in one.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what may be done with that land. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
